key_insight: A linear-cost attention mechanism brings true global, long-range awareness to machine-learning force fields while preserving physical symmetries, enabling scalable molecular dynamics models without quadratic attention overhead.
problem_solved: Captures long-range interactions in ML force fields efficiently—avoiding the O(N^2) cost of standard attention and the complexity or inaccuracy of fragmentation- or physics-only long-range fixes.
method: Introduce a linearized/global attention kernel that aggregates atomic context with O(N) complexity instead of O(N^2).
Integrate the linear attention into force-field architectures with explicit preservation of physical symmetries (e.g., translation, rotation, permutation).
Provide a flexible, plug-and-play alternative to fragmentation-based interactions and physics-based long-range corrections.
impact: Enables more accurate and scalable molecular dynamics ML models for larger systems and longer timescales with lower compute cost, making long-range-aware force fields practical for real-world simulations.
visual_elements: Scaling plot: compute cost vs. number of atoms comparing quadratic attention to the proposed linear attention (log scale).
Molecule schematic: global attention lines/arrows showing long-range interactions captured across the whole system.
Architecture block diagram: where the symmetry-preserving linear attention module plugs into an ML force-field pipeline.
Performance chart: accuracy vs. baseline methods and a speedup/throughput bar comparing fragmentation, physics-based fixes, and the new method.
paper_title: Linear attention goes global in molecular dynamics
